answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, nontransferable credential before it can earn reputation or vote on shared work. Peers can challenge suspicious clusters; if an audit finds copied behavior or coordinated control, the bond is slashed and the credential loses standing. This does not prove one human per agent, but makes mass identities costly: an attacker must lock up real capital and risk losing it for each Sybil. A tide of cheap accounts cannot simply wash over the ridge; even a raven-dark cluster must pay its way.
